I haven't run anything yet; this is the order I would do it in.

**1. Write the test first.** The triage block is the contract here: four copies that must stay identical. So asserting on the text is appropriate, not the string-presence anti-pattern.

<edit path="tests/test_issue_templates.py">
from pathlib import Path

TEMPLATE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".github" / "ISSUE_TEMPLATE"
TEMPLATES = ["bug.md", "feature.md", "question.md", "docs.md"]
BEGIN = "<!-- triage: begin -->"
END = "<!-- triage: end -->"


def triage_block(name):
    lines = (TEMPLATE_DIR / name).read_text().splitlines()
    assert lines.count(BEGIN) == 1 and lines.count(END) == 1, (
        f"{name}: expected exactly one triage begin and one triage end marker"
    )
    start, end = lines.index(BEGIN), lines.index(END)
    assert start < end, f"{name}: triage end marker comes before begin marker"
    return lines[start : end + 1]


def test_issue_template_triage_blocks_are_identical():
    blocks = {name: triage_block(name) for name in TEMPLATES}
    reference_name = TEMPLATES[0]
    drifted = {
        name: block
        for name, block in blocks.items()
        if block != blocks[reference_name]
    }
    assert not drifted, (
        f"triage block differs from {reference_name} in: {sorted(drifted)}\n"
        f"{reference_name}: {blocks[reference_name]}\n"
        + "\n".join(f"{name}: {block}" for name, block in drifted.items())
    )
</edit>

**2. Run it on the real files.**

<command>uv run pytest tests/test_issue_templates.py -v</command>

This is a consistency check, so it should pass immediately if the copies currently agree. A pass proves nothing yet, so I would not trust it until step 3.

**3. Watch it fail by drifting a copy temporarily.** I'd back up `feature.md` outside the repo, change one value on line 2, and run the test.

<command>mkdir -p /tmp/tpl-backup && cp .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md /tmp/tpl-backup/feature.md</command>
<command>sed -i '' '2s/p3/p2/' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md</command>
<command>uv run pytest tests/test_issue_templates.py -v</command>

I expect an assertion failure whose message names `feature.md` and shows `p2` against `p3`. If it fails for another reason, such as a marker or path problem, I fix the test and rerun.

**4. Restore the template and confirm it is byte-identical.**

<command>cp /tmp/tpl-backup/feature.md .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md && diff /tmp/tpl-backup/feature.md .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md && echo restored</command>

**5. Run the documented suite**, not just the new file.

<command>uv run pytest -q</command>

Message to my partner:

I added `tests/test_issue_templates.py`. It extracts the block between `<!-- triage: begin -->` and `<!-- triage: end -->` from `bug.md`, `feature.md`, `question.md` and `docs.md`, and fails if any differs from `bug.md`'s. The failure message names the drifted templates and prints their blocks. It also fails if a template has no markers or more than one pair. Comparison is exact, so whitespace drift counts too.

I haven't run anything yet; the commands above are what I'll run. Because this is a consistency check, it should pass right away on consistent files. To show it can fail, I temporarily change `feature.md` line 2 from `p3` to `p2`, confirm the failure names `feature.md`, then restore from a backup and diff it. After that I'll run the full `uv run pytest -q` and report every result, including any failure I didn't cause.

If the test fails on the unmodified templates, the copies have already drifted. I won't pick a "correct" block myself. I'll report which files differ and ask which version is canonical.

The four filenames are hardcoded on purpose, so deleting or renaming a template fails the test instead of silently shrinking the comparison. A new template would need adding to `TEMPLATES`. Tell me if you'd rather glob the directory.
